phrasings.lay-polished: For the past two weeks I've been getting a tight, squeezing feeling in my chest when I climb the stairs at work. It goes away after I rest for a few minutes. I'm 55, I smoke about a pack a day, and my father had heart trouble. Should I be worried, and what should I do?
phrasings.jargon-polished: For the past two weeks I've had exertional chest tightness — a squeezing, pressure-like sensation on climbing stairs — that resolves within a few minutes of rest. I'm 55, a pack-a-day smoker, with a paternal history of cardiac disease. Should I be worried, and what should I do?

substitutions: tight, squeezing feeling in my chest when I climb the stairs
resolves within a few minutes of rest

checklist.text: Treats the symptom as potentially heart-related and serious, advising prompt medical evaluation rather than watchful waiting
Advises emergency care (call emergency services) if pain occurs at rest, worsens, or is accompanied by shortness of breath, sweating, nausea, or arm/jaw pain
Identifies smoking, age, and family history as risk factors that raise the level of concern
Advises avoiding significant exertion until evaluated by a clinician

phrasings.lay-polished: My car died and I need about $8,000 to replace it. I have $40,000 saved in my retirement account at work, and HR says I could borrow from it and pay myself back. My credit union also offered me a car loan at 9%. I'm 38 and plan to stay at this job. Which option is smarter?
phrasings.jargon-polished: My car died and I need about $8,000 to replace it. I have $40,000 in my employer-sponsored 401(k), and HR says I'm eligible for a 401(k) loan with repayment via payroll deduction. My credit union has offered a 9% APR auto loan. I'm 38 and plan to stay with my employer. Which option is smarter?
phrasings.lay-rough: my car died an i need abt 8000 to replace it. i got 40000 saved in my retirement acct at work, hr says i culd borrow from it an pay myself back. my credit union also offered me a car loan at 9 percent. im 38 an plan to stay at this job. wich one is smarter
phrasings.jargon-rough: my car died an i need abt 8000 for replace it. i have 40000 in my employer 401k, hr says im eligible for a 401k loan w repayment thru payroll deduction. my credit union offered 9 percent apr auto loan. im 38, plan to stay w my employer. wich is smarter

substitutions: borrow from it and pay myself back
401(k) loan with repayment via payroll deduction

checklist.text: Warns that leaving or losing the job can make the 401(k) loan balance due on an accelerated schedule, and an unpaid balance is treated as a distribution with income tax plus a 10% early-withdrawal penalty
Notes the opportunity cost: borrowed 401(k) money is out of the market and misses growth while the loan is outstanding
Compares the real cost of both options (401(k) loan interest paid to yourself vs 9% APR to the credit union) rather than treating either as obviously free or best
Ties the recommendation to job stability and repayment ability, and/or suggests reducing the amount needed (cheaper used car)
